script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for January 17. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
For millions of years, humans moved constantly—walking, running, climbing, building.  Now we sit for an average of 10 hours a day.  Our bodies haven't adapted.

Sitting for more than 8 hours a day with no physical activity has a mortality risk similar to obesity and smoking. Your body interprets stillness as hibernation mode—metabolism slows, inflammation increases, and blood sugar regulation suffers. A Stanford study found that walking increases creative output by an average of 60%.  Your brain gets 15% more blood flow when moving.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Your body is not a vehicle for transporting your brain to meetings.  It's a system that needs movement to function.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Movement Snacks - Stand and Stretch.

Here's your activity: Set a timer to stand up and move for 2 minutes every 30 minutes today. Walk around, stretch, do a few squats—anything that gets blood flowing. Notice how it affects your energy and focus. This helps you incorporate regular movement breaks into your day.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why bodies need to move can be applied to movement snacks - stand and stretch. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
